skills.name: Establish compatible fractional form
skills.definition: Prepare operands so fractional parts are in a subtraction-ready form by finding a common denominator and converting to equivalent fractions when needed.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because denominator alignment is a distinct preparation skill with its own error pattern and is not always required in problems where operands are already compatible.

skills.name: Rewrite operands into subtraction-ready form
skills.definition: Rewrite whole numbers or nonstandard mixed numbers into a form suitable for subtraction, such as adding a zero fractional part or normalizing an improper fractional part.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because operand rewriting is a preparation skill different from denominator alignment and borrowing; students may need this even when no common denominator is required.

skills.name: Subtract and regroup
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction of aligned whole-number and fractional parts, including handling intermediate negative fractional differences and regrouping by borrowing from the whole part when necessary.
skills.merge_rationale: Merged because borrowing is tightly coupled to the subtraction execution phase. In the dossiers, S04 appears only as a continuation of subtraction after an initial aligned-parts attempt. Since S04 has S03 as a prerequisite and functions as a repair within the same computational operation, combining them preserves meaningful diagnosis at a coarser level.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or convert zero-valued fractional forms into 0 or an equivalent integer form when appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is a finalization skill with distinct error patterns from subtraction and recombination; students often compute correctly but fail to reduce.

skills.name: Express final answer
skills.definition: Present the final value in standard form by combining whole and fractional parts into a mixed number, fraction, or integer as appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because recombining parts into a final answer is a distinct representational step, especially in mixed-number items, and can be correct or incorrect independently of simplification.

skills.name: Prepare operands for subtraction
skills.definition: Set up the numbers in subtraction-ready form by rewriting operands as needed and establishing compatible fractional parts, including common-denominator conversion when required.
skills.merge_rationale: This merges the two preparation skills because both are setup operations that occur before core subtraction and serve the same instructional phase: making operands compatible for subtraction.

skills.name: Subtract and regroup
skills.definition: Compute the difference by subtracting aligned whole and fractional parts and regrouping by borrowing when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
skills.merge_rationale: Retained as a merged execution cluster because subtraction and borrowing form a single computational phase; borrowing is a conditional extension of subtraction rather than an independent phase.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or convert zero-valued fractional forms into 0 or an equivalent integer form when appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate at K=4 to preserve the distinction between numerical reduction and answer formatting; students may simplify incorrectly even when they can express the answer form.

skills.name: Express final answer
skills.definition: Present the final value in standard form as an appropriate mixed number, fraction, or integer after computation.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate at K=4 to preserve the representational final step, which can vary independently from simplification and remains instructionally meaningful.

aggregation_notes: Repaired the invalid K=4 codebook by ensuring every skill has at least one original_skill_id and that the number of skills matches target_k. Aggregation follows problem-solving phases: setup, execution, simplification, and final expression. At K=5, only S03 and S04 are merged because borrowing is best treated as part of subtraction execution. At K=4, S01 and S02 are merged into a single preparation skill, while S05 and S06 remain separate so the codebook still contains exactly four substantive, fully mapped skills.
